risk_metrics.label: Daily volatility
risk_metrics.description: Sample standard deviation (n-1) of daily simple returns.

risk_metrics.label: Annualized volatility
risk_metrics.description: Daily volatility x sqrt(252). The 252 trading days per year is a convention, not a measurement.

risk_metrics.label: Maximum drawdown
risk_metrics.description: Largest peak-to-trough fall of the close: close / running peak - 1 (negative).

risk_metrics.label: Current drawdown
risk_metrics.description: Latest close / highest close in the window - 1 (0 at a new high).

risk_metrics.label: Historical VaR (95%)
risk_metrics.description: 5th percentile of daily returns (linear interpolation). -0.02 = a 2% one-day loss or worse on ~5% of days.

risk_metrics.label: Historical CVaR (95%)
risk_metrics.description: Mean of the daily returns at or below the historical VaR.

risk_metrics.label: Beta vs benchmark
risk_metrics.description: cov(asset, benchmark) / var(benchmark) of returns between consecutive common dates.

risk_metrics.label: Correlation vs benchmark
risk_metrics.description: Pearson correlation of the same aligned returns.

formulas: component score = weighted mean of its available indicator sub-scores (equal weights among those available)
effective component weight = configured weight / sum of configured weights of the components that contribute
overall score = sum over contributing components of (effective weight * component score)
rules: An indicator that is missing is excluded and the remaining indicators of that component are re-weighted; it is never filled in, defaulted, or treated as 0 or 50.
A component needs at least its stated minimum number of available indicators, otherwise it is unavailable.
The overall score needs at least 2 contributing components and at least 50% of the configured weight; otherwise it is null with the reason.
A component with weight 0 is shown but does not contribute.
Values are taken from the stored results of earlier phases exactly as stored; nothing is recomputed or repaired.
Only the latest complete result of each phase is used; the date each input is as-of is reported and no age-based discounting is applied.
limits: This is an educational summary, not investment advice. It does not recommend buying, selling, or holding anything and says nothing about future returns.
The reference anchors are illustrative round numbers, not calibrated on data, industries, or market regimes; the same ratio can be ordinary in one sector and alarming in another.
'Favourable' encodes design assumptions (for example, lower volatility is preferred). They are choices, not findings, and a different investor objective would justify different anchors.
Equal weights are a no-information default, not evidence that the components matter equally. Changing the weights changes the score by exactly the amounts shown.
The score has not been backtested or validated against outcomes; no predictive power is claimed.
A score built from fewer components or indicators is less informative; always read the reported coverage.

The score inherits the limits of every input phase: prices are unadjusted for splits and dividends, sentiment accuracy has not been measured, fundamentals are only as good as the uploaded file, and live market and news data have never been fetched in testing.
Inputs can come from different dates or different price snapshots; their as-of dates are reported but not reconciled.

steps: Step 1 - Each indicator value is read exactly as stored by the earlier phase; nothing is recomputed or repaired.
Step 2 - Each value becomes a 0-100 sub-score: 100 x clamp((value - poor) / (good - poor), 0, 1). The value at the 'poor' anchor scores 0, at the 'good' anchor 100, linear in between, flat beyond.
Step 3 - A component score is the equal-weighted mean of the sub-scores that are available; a missing indicator is dropped and the rest are re-weighted, never filled in.

Step 4 - Component weights (default equal): Fundamentals 25.0%, Technical (trend position) 25.0%, Sentiment 25.0%, Risk (realised) 25.0%. Components that are unavailable or weight 0 are left out and the remaining weights are rescaled to sum to 100%.
Step 5 - The overall score is the sum of (effective weight x component score) over contributing components.

steps: Step 1 - Each indicator value is read exactly as stored by the earlier phase; nothing is recomputed or repaired.
Step 2 - Each value becomes a 0-100 sub-score: 100 x clamp((value - poor) / (good - poor), 0, 1). The value at the 'poor' anchor scores 0, at the 'good' anchor 100, linear in between, flat beyond.
Step 3 - A component score is the equal-weighted mean of the sub-scores that are available; a missing indicator is dropped and the rest are re-weighted, never filled in.

Step 4 - Component weights (default equal): Fundamentals 25.0%, Technical (trend position) 25.0%, Sentiment 25.0%, Risk (realised) 25.0%. Components that are unavailable or weight 0 are left out and the remaining weights are rescaled to sum to 100%.
Step 5 - The overall score is the sum of (effective weight x component score) over contributing components.
